page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance includes 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It carries no local storage, relying on external cloud block devices, and includes no discrete GPU accelerators. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance consistently in the average middle 50 percent range across standard computing metrics. It scores 1417.0 points in single-core and 5300.0 points in multi-core Geekbench tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 10427.92 and stress-ng throughput of 7717.41 multi-core operations. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 60.16 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 42.66 GB/sec. Application tests register 7.81 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 9.56 GB/sec. Because it lacks accelerator hardware, large language model performance drops significantly on heavier models, posting 15.99 tokens per second on 7B prompt processing and 7.29 tokens per second during generation.

With its dedicated core execution and standard balance of compute and memory, ecs.u1-c1m4.2xlarge provides predictable performance for non-bursty enterprise software without the premium associated with specialized memory or high-frequency compute nodes. It is suitable for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, caching services, and intermediate database workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 32.0 GB of RAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it features AVX-512 and AES vector and cryptographic instructions alongside 33 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance benchmarks position the system squarely in the middle 50 percent across standard CPU and memory tests, scoring 5300.0 on Geekbench multi-core and handling 7.81 million Redis SET operations per second. Its balanced resource footprint delivers dependable CPU density for standard web applications, intermediate databases, build servers, and containerized microservices.
